title: Thomas and Sylvester: believe with the heart = by will (Romans 10:10)
source_text: XXVI. Quibus conformia sunt quae scribit Thomas Aquinas in illa verba Pauli, Corde enim creditur ad justitiam. Corde creditur, inquit, id est, voluntate. Nam caetera quae ad exteriorem Dei cultum pertinent, potest homo nolens; sed credere non potest, nisi volens. Intellectus enim credentis non determinatur ad assentiendum veritati, ex necessitate rationis, sicut intellectus scientis, sed ex voluntate. Et in eadem verba Sylvester: Ait corde credere, ad excludendam fictionem, cum qua multi accedunt ad Baptismum, & ad indicandum quod fides conferens justitiam a voluntate imperatur, ad differentiam fidei coactae, qualis est in daemonibus, & erat in illis qui crediderunt in eum a signis coacti, ipse autem Christus non credebat semetipsum eis. Nam haec fides justitiam non affert: nam ut scientia virtute rationis demonstrantis gignitur, ita fides non demonstratur, sed virtute suscipitur voluntatis captivantis intellectum in obsequium Christi, qui illam infundit.
pass_a_gloss: Conformable to this are what Thomas Aquinas writes on those words of Paul, For with the heart one believes unto righteousness (Romans 10:10). With the heart one believes, he says, that is, by the will. For other things that belong to the outward worship of God a man can do unwilling; but he cannot believe unless willing. For the believer's intellect is not determined to assenting to truth by necessity of reason, as the knower's intellect is, but from the will. And on the same words Sylvester: He says believe with the heart, to exclude fiction with which many approach Baptism, and to indicate that faith conferring righteousness is commanded by the will, unto difference from coerced faith such as is in demons, and was in those who believed in Him coerced by signs, yet Christ did not entrust Himself to them. For this faith does not bring righteousness: for as science is begotten by the force of demonstrating reason, so faith is not demonstrated but is received by the force of the will capturing the intellect into the obedience of Christ, who infuses it.
pass_b_english: Thomas on Romans 10:10: believing with the heart = by the will; one can do outward cult unwilling, but not believe.
Sylvester: heart-belief excludes fiction and marks will-commanded saving faith vs coerced demonic/sign-faith (Romans 10:10).

lemmas.gloss: For with the heart one believes

choices.why: Cult can be forced; faith cannot.
